author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read syslog from Yamaha RTX and NVR routers, and FWX120 and SRT100: filter, NAT and [INSPECT] logs, intrusion detection, URL filter and login lines. The routers send it to the data collector. Filter, NAT and [INSPECT] connection logs go to Netflow, intrusion detection lines to NIDS, URL filter lines to HTTP and logins to Auth.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the data collector with syslog host <address>, turn on syslog notice (filter, [INSPECT], intrusion detection and URL filter logs) and keep syslog info on (logins).
- Set syslog format type rfc3164 or rfc5424 where the firmware has it (RTX1300, RTX1220, RTX1210, RTX830, RTX840, vRX and NVR510 on 2024 or later firmware).
- Filters log with reject (reject-log) or pass-log; ip filter dynamic logs a summary of each connection.

Field mapping:
- IP filter and NAT logs (Passed or Rejected at IN, OUT or NAT) go to Netflow with the interface, filter and detail, and [INSPECT] connection summaries go to Netflow as allowed with the start time, the arrow giving which end opened the connection.
- Intrusion detection lines ([INSPECT] <attack> <src> > <dst>) go to NIDS with the attack name; the line gives no action.
- URL filter lines go to HTTP with the URL, client and filter.
- Logins, failures, logouts, administrator mode and lockouts on TELNET, SSH, HTTP, Serial and Remote, local or through RADIUS, go to Auth.

Time:
- The default format sends no time or host name, so those lines keep the ingest time.
- The rfc3164 time has no zone and is read as UTC; rfc5424 carries the offset.

Sources and licenses:
- How sure this is: the message text comes from Yamaha's Japanese technical docs, FAQ and release notes on Yamaha's RTpro site; the messages themselves are English.
- The filter, [INSPECT], intrusion detection and RADIUS and HTTP login lines appear there as examples or templates.
- How the URL filter writes the interface and direction is inferred, and so is the exact text of a local SSH or console login beyond the Syslog FAQ's list.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in those shapes.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 (185 of 186 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (185 of 186 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs).
- The one difference is the event time of the default-format line, which has none: both take the ingest time, and the emulator's is reference_time.
- No built-in parser competed for these lines.

Known gaps:
- IKE and IPsec (debug level only), L2TP, PPP, DPI and config saves aren't covered.
- IPv6 filter lines aren't documented and aren't read.
